utils.check_docstrings module¶

Docstring Compliance Checker.

This script traverses Python files in specified directories or file paths, parses them using the ast module, and checks for the presence of docstrings in modules, classes, and functions.

It identifies missing docstrings to help maintain documentation standards across the codebase.

Usage:

python check_docstrings.py <path1> [path2 …]

utils.check_docstrings.check_docstrings_recursive(directory)[source]¶

Recursively check a directory for Python files with missing docstrings.

Parameters:

directory (str) – The root directory to search.

Returns:

A list of strings describing missing docstrings in all found Python files.

Return type:

list

utils.check_docstrings.check_path(path)[source]¶

Check a single file for missing docstrings using AST parsing.

Parameters:

path (str) – The file path to check.

Returns:

A list of strings describing any missing docstrings found.

Returns an empty list if the file is not a Python file, has syntax errors, or is fully documented.

Return type:

list

utils.model_versioning module¶

Model versioning and artifact management for NGLab.

This module provides utilities for saving, loading, and managing model versions with comprehensive metadata for reproducibility and experiment tracking.

class utils.model_versioning.ModelRegistry(base_path: str | Path)[source]¶

Bases: object

Registry for managing multiple model versions.

Provides a centralized interface for saving, loading, and listing models.

Example

>>> registry = ModelRegistry("models/")
>>> registry.save(model, "vae", "1.0.0", metadata)
>>> model = registry.load("vae", "1.0.0")
>>> versions = registry.list_versions("vae")

utils.model_versioning.check_version_compatibility(current_version: str, checkpoint_version: str) → bool[source]¶

Check if checkpoint version is compatible with current code.

Uses semantic versioning: major.minor.patch - Major version mismatch: incompatible - Minor/patch mismatch: compatible with warning

Parameters:

  • current_version – Current model version

  • checkpoint_version – Checkpoint version

Returns:

True if compatible, False otherwise

utils.model_versioning.load_model_with_metadata(model: Module, load_path: str | Path, map_location: str | device | None = None, strict: bool = True) → tuple[Module, ModelMetadata][source]¶

Load model checkpoint with metadata.

Parameters:

  • model – Model instance to load state into

  • load_path – Path to checkpoint

  • map_location – Device to load tensors to

  • strict – Whether to strictly enforce state_dict keys match

Returns:

Tuple of (loaded_model, metadata)

Example

>>> model = VAE(input_dim=10, latent_dim=64)
>>> model, metadata = load_model_with_metadata(model, "checkpoints/vae_v1.pt")
>>> print(f"Loaded model version {metadata.version}")
utils.model_versioning.save_model_with_metadata(model: Module, save_path: str | Path, metadata: ModelMetadata, optimizer: Optimizer | None = None, scheduler: Any | None = None) → None[source]¶

Save model checkpoint with comprehensive metadata.

Parameters:

  • model – PyTorch model to save

  • save_path – Path to save checkpoint

  • metadata – Model metadata

  • optimizer – Optimizer state (optional)

  • scheduler – Learning rate scheduler state (optional)

Example

>>> metadata = ModelMetadata(
...     version="1.0.0",
...     model_type="VAE",
...     framework_version=f"pytorch-{torch.__version__}",
...     hyperparameters={"latent_dim": 64},
...     metrics={"val_loss": 0.123},
...     training_date=datetime.now().isoformat(),
...     dataset_hash=compute_dataset_hash("data/train.csv"),
... )
>>> save_model_with_metadata(model, "checkpoints/vae_v1.pt", metadata)
